headline: Agent research study reports a 10% average gain from periodically resetting search history
summary: An October 14 preprint tests a simple reset rule for iterative agent research: after each round, discard every agent session and candidate history, then restart a communicating team from the best candidate and its score. Across four tasks in heuristic programming, kernel optimization and small-model training, four-agent teams with three resets reportedly improved mean best results by 10% over four parallel agents and 22% over one continuing agent, at the same total token cost. Each configuration used one model and was run three times per task. The authors attribute the gains to renewed exploration after sessions become anchored to prior attempts. These are author-reported benchmark results from a single agent/model harness, not an independent replication or evidence that forgetting is universally beneficial.
